title: Richard White
text:
I am a bioinformatician in the Busch Lab at Queen Mary University of London and have a PhD in developmental biology from the University of London.
After my PhD, I travelled to California to work in the lab of Tom Schilling at the University of California, Irvine. I spent 5 years working on retinoic acid signalling in zebrafish development and trying to learn to surf.
In 2011, I made the switch from wet lab to bioinformatics and joined the Zebrafish Mutation Project at the Wellcome Sanger Institute. Since then, I have worked on software to automate CRISPR/Cas9 experiments and large scale RNA-seq studies on early zebrafish and mouse development.
I write in R, Python and Perl and I love making plots.

title: Making this website
text:
The initial steps are from this YouTube tutorial.
Briefly, I created a new Quarto Blog project in Rstudio, which creates a set of template files to start with. The index.qmd file is formatted as a blog, so I renamed it to blog.qmd. Then I renamed the about.qmd file to index.qmd to use as the site home page. Then I updated the _quarto.yml file to add a nav bar to the left hand side as shown in the video. And I removed the example blog posts as well. I also added a line to change the directory where the website is created when it is rendered. This is done by adding this line to the project section of _quarto.yml
  output-dir: "docs"
Now, when I render the website, it is created in a docs folder. The default theme is Cosmo, which I kept, but I also added a optional dark theme, Superhero
Once the initial set up was done, I set about customising the Home page by editing the index.qmd file.
First, I added a profile picture. Initially, the index.qmd file has a default profile picture profile.jpg. I created an assets folder and an images folder within that. In there, I put a picture of me named profile.jpg and I changed the filename in the YAML to assets/images/profile.jpg.
Then in the index.qmd file, I added some text about me and some images. The images were also placed in the assets/images folder. An image is normally rendered as a block element on its own line, but I wanted to have all three on the same line. So, I put them inside a div element using
::: {#example-plots style="background-color: #FFFFFF"}
![](assets/images/zfs-fig1b.png){width=30%}
![](assets/images/top1000-var-high-res.png){width=30%}
![](assets/images/shigella-heatmap.png){width=30%}
:::
I made sure the images all fitted by adding {width=30%}.
The style="background-color: #FFFFFF" makes sure there is a consistent background in dark mode.
Finally,I wanted to remove the link to the bin fire that is Twitter and change it to Bluesky and add a link to my ORCiD page. This has a list of my publications. The Bluesky and ORCiD icons are not in the standard bootstrap icons, but are provided in the set of free FontAwesome icons. So I installed the Quarto Font Awesome extension
quarto add quarto-ext/fontawesome
The Bluesky and ORCiD logos are in the brands set, so the shortcodes for them are:
{{< fa brands bluesky >}}
{{< fa brands orcid >}}
A slight wrinkle is that instead of using the icon key as in the github and twitter examples, you need to use the text key, as explained here.
So the yaml in the frontmatter of the index.qmd file looks like this:
title: "Richard White"
image: assets/images/profile.jpg
about:
  template: jolla
  links:
    - icon: github
      text: Github
      href: https://github.com/richysix
    - text: "{{< fa brands bluesky >}} Bluesky"
      href: https://bsky.app/profile/richysix.bsky.social
    - text: "{{< fa brands orcid >}} ORCiD"
      href: https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1842-412X
And the buttons look like this:
 
There are similar links in the _quarto.yml file for the nav bar.
